newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo dinar black market rate back to 3.8.
newsitem.headline: Yugo dinar black market rate back to 3.8.

text.p: Yugoslavia's dinar extended gains on Monday with the black market rate returning to its pre-New Year level of 3.8 to the German mark, dealers said.
The dinar stood at 4.00 to the mark on Sunday.
"Whoever flooded the streets with freshly printed dinar banknotes withdrew them over past few days and the dinar is almost back to normal," one street dealer told Reuters.

The plunge in the dinar black market rate started during the eight-day New Year and Christmas holidays after a substantial monetary expansion in the last few days of 1996 ended up in the streets of Belgrade and many other Serbian towns.
The dinar hit its low of 4.3 to the mark in Belgrade, with dealers asking as much as five dinars to sell the mark. But even at a price so high, they were reluctant to sell.
Analysts said it was the fourth such toppling of the dinar since January 1994, when the new "super dinar" was launched in an attempt to put an end to the hyperinflation running at 60 percent a day.
Economists saw the latest attack on the dinar as a deliberate move by the Serbian government to cover its burgeoning fiscal gap.

Some analysts cautioned the whole operation was conducted with the help of several big commercial banks, which kept their balances in the red. They estimated between 500 million and one billion dinars were printed for those purposes.

"This is not the way to govern the country and its economy," a source close to the central bank said. "There must be no devaluation, otherwise it would bury the essence of the entire economic programme."
After the unfortunate episode of the sinking dinar, the federal government and the central bank issued late on Friday statements reiterating their commitment to currency and price stability.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia said in a press release it would take decisive measures to stabilize the dinar and restore financial discipline.

Sources close to the central bank said it would even liquidate insolvent banks if the current set of measures gives no result. But the bank did not elaborate its steps. The dinar officially remains fixed at 3.3 to the German mark.

The Belgrade daily Nasa Borba, quoting a source close to the federal government, said the central bank and the government agreed on Friday to postpone the dinar devaluation until mid-March. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
